findings.title: Privileged workflows execute mutable GitHub Action tags
findings.where: The cited `uses:` entries select `actions/checkout@v6`, `actions/setup-node@v6`, or `actions/github-script@v9` rather than immutable commit SHAs.
findings.what: A mutable upstream tag can resolve to different code without a repository change. These actions consequently run with each job's token, workspace, and deployment-secret access, weakening supply-chain reproducibility and allowing an upstream tag compromise to affect write-capable or publishing workflows.
findings.fix: Replace every external major-version action reference with the reviewed 40-character commit SHA for that release, retaining the version in a comment for update tooling.
findings.acceptance: A workflow-policy check parses all seven files and confirms every non-local `uses:` value is pinned to a full 40-hex commit SHA; rerunning it produces no violations.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read every `uses:` entry at the immutable baseline. The peaceiris deployment action is already pinned and was excluded; only the mutable actions/* references cited above survive.

findings.title: Stable publisher executes an unverified latest-version CLI archive
findings.where: The bootstrap step resolves the current latest gh release, streams its archive directly into tar, and places the extracted executable on GITHUB_PATH.
findings.what: The deployed tool version changes independently of this checkout, and the downloaded archive is neither checksum- nor signature-verified before its executable is used with GITHUB_TOKEN. TLS does not provide artifact immutability or release-asset integrity, so compromise or replacement of the upstream release path can become code execution in the stable publishing job.
findings.fix: Pin an explicit gh version and expected SHA-256 digest, download the archive to a temporary file, verify it with `sha256sum -c`, and only then extract and add its binary directory to GITHUB_PATH; alternatively use a reviewed SHA-pinned installer action with equivalent verification.
findings.acceptance: A controlled run succeeds with the pinned archive, then a test substituting an incorrect expected digest fails before extraction or execution; the workflow no longer queries `/releases/latest`.
findings.verifyNote: Re-read lines 54-66 at baseline: `set -euo pipefail` and `curl -f` cover transport/process failures but there is no digest, signature, immutable version, or verification step before the extracted binary is exposed for subsequent authenticated use.
